title: Police probe unit biased, says relative of dead man
article: The father-in-law of a man who died after an altercation with police in 2008, during which a Taser stun gun was used, says such incidents are still happening too frequently.

"It's truly ironic to see the headlines from a couple of days ago. It still goes on," John Chernekoff told reporters outside court following the opening day of a fatality inquiry into the death of Gordon Walker Bowe. "There will be no end to (these types of incidents) until someone is held accountable."

A city police officer who shot and killed 40-year-old Corey Peeace on Friday had deployed a Taser on the man during a domestic assault call in February 2010 at the home in the 200 block of Erin Meadow Close S.E.
Chernekoff accused the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) of being biased because it relies on police information and is made up of police members.

ASIRT investigated the actions of four Calgary police officers in the death of the Castlegar, B.C., resident, who travelled back and forth to Calgary for work, and reported nine months later there would be no charges laid.
ASIRT concluded Bowe, 30, was high on cocaine and died of excited delirium and not as a the result of a Taser or police actions.
Executive director Clifton Purvis said he came to his decision after reviewing the investigation, consulting with the medical examiner and considering the opinion of the Crown's office.
Chernekoff said he and other family members are attending the fatality inquiry to "learn more about what happened."
The incident started on Nov. 1, 2008, when police were called to a break and enter. When they arrived, Bowe was found in an unoccupied basement being renovated on 42nd Street S.E.

A struggle ensued with police and a Taser was deployed, although it was not clear if it actually zapped him. Police soon noticed Bowe was in medical distress and he was rushed to hospital, where he died the next day.
Chernekoff has been skeptical of police from the start, telling the Herald days after the death that the man's bruising seemed, in his opinion, to be the result of a severe beating.
Bowe was just hours from returning home to B.C. He packed his bags and called home to say he was soon on his way, his family said.
But for some reason, Bowe ended up in the vacant basement.
Bowe lived with his common-law wife in Castlegar and together they were raising two young children.
A fatality inquiry cannot find fault, but the judge can make recommendations to prevent similar incidents.
